item.title: Behavioural Environmental Economics & Policy (BEEP): trends and reflections
item.content:encoded:
Sanchayan Banerjee, King's College London

Lory Barile, University of Warwick

This special issue focuses on Behavioural Environmental Economics & Policy (BEEP), which examines how departures from rational choice assumptions—such as bounded rationality and bounded willpower—affect environmental decision-making and policy effectiveness. The issue seeks to consolidate evidence on how behavioural insights can improve the design and evaluation of environmental policies to address urgent challenges including climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution.

The special issue welcomes conceptual, empirical, and policy-oriented contributions applying behavioural insights to environmental problems. Submissions may employ various methodologies including experiments, quasi-experimental designs, and literature reviews. The issue particularly values work that identifies both market and behavioural failures, designs and tests policies combining traditional instruments with behavioural tools, and evaluates their effectiveness and welfare impacts.

This is an invitation-only special issue in Environmental and Resource Economics.

Appel publié par Environmental and Resource Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Interactions between market failures and behavioural failures in environmental settings
  • Policy design that combines prices/standards with behavioural tools (defaults, salience/framing, simplification, commitment)
  • Welfare analysis (including psychological costs), ethics, and paternalism in environmental policy
  • Empirical identification of behavioural mechanisms; field/lab/quasi-experimental evidence
  • Heterogeneity, equity, and distributional consequences of behavioural environmental policies
  • Replication, meta-analysis, and open-science practices in this domain
  • Choice architecture and environmental outcomes
  • Interactions between behavioural instruments and prices/regulation
  • Climate cognition and communication
  • Evaluation and methods

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Valuing health and longevity: Advances and innovations
item.content:encoded:
Lisa A. Robinson, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

Olof Bystrom, OECD

Ståle Navrud, Norwegian University of Life Sciences

This special issue focuses on the economic valuation of health risks and mortality in the context of environmental policy. Mortality risks dominate benefit estimates in environmental policies, but the value per statistical life literature contains significant gaps regarding how population and risk characteristics affect valuations. Similarly, nonfatal health impacts receive limited attention despite their substantial magnitude, and methodological challenges persist in synthesizing estimates across studies and applying them to new contexts.

The collection addresses recent advances in measuring individual willingness to pay for both mortality and morbidity risk reductions, improved techniques for combining and transferring results across research settings, and innovations in addressing practical questions such as how to handle co-occurring health effects and distributional equity concerns. The special issue brings together important contributions that serve as a reference for researchers and practitioners applying economic valuation methods to health and longevity improvements.

Appel publié par Environmental and Resource Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Value per statistical life (VSL) and mortality risk reductions in environmental policy
  • Population and risk attributes affecting valuation estimates
  • Synthesis and application of VSL estimates across studies and contexts
  • Valuation of nonfatal risk reductions and morbidity impacts
  • Willingness to pay (WTP) methods for mortality and morbidity outcomes
  • Approaches for combining and transferring valuation estimates
  • Addressing equity and distributional concerns in health valuation
  • Cost-benefit analysis methods for environmental and health policies
  • Best practice approaches to health and longevity valuation

Timeline

  • October 31, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Market-Based Measures for Port and Shipping Emissions Mitigation
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on market-based measures and economic instruments designed to mitigate emissions from ports and the shipping industry. The collection seeks to advance understanding of how market mechanisms can effectively reduce environmental impacts while maintaining economic competitiveness in the maritime sector.

The issue welcomes contributions exploring various market-based approaches including carbon pricing, emission trading systems, green bonds, subsidies for clean technologies, and other economic instruments. Papers may examine these mechanisms from theoretical, empirical, or policy perspectives, with particular interest in their effectiveness, design, implementation challenges, and real-world outcomes.

Appel publié par Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Market-based mechanisms for reducing port and shipping emissions
  • Carbon pricing and emission trading systems in maritime transport
  • Economic instruments for incentivizing sustainable shipping practices
  • Port authority policies and market-based approaches
  • Life cycle assessment and environmental impact of shipping
  • Technological innovations and market adoption in emissions reduction
  • Regulatory frameworks and market-based policy integration
  • Case studies of successful market-based emissions mitigation strategies

Timeline

  • August 28, 2026: Manuscript submission deadline
